content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing near-term price momentum.
- After sharp spikes in true values (e.g., 60+), forecasts overshoot initially but then fall short — indicating poor handling of volatility clustering.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: overestimates after low points and underestimates after high points — likely due to insufficient momentum capture.
- Forecasts for the last 5–10 days are often too low, suggesting underweighting of recent upward trends or overreaction to short-term volatility.
- Model fails to anticipate sustained upward trends in the latter half of the forecast horizon — particularly when true values rise above 60–70.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the early part of the horizon, underestimating the “rebound” effect after low points.
- Model exhibits a tendency to “smooth” sharp transitions — underestimating sudden spikes and overestimating gradual declines.
